On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 08:23, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Claire — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm pulling our on-call SREs in now and will coordinate a mitigations plan.

Claire / team — quick findings from the first log samples:
- ~75% of 5xx responses are 502/503 from the frontend edge experiencing transient OOMs on large-attention models after a sudden concurrency burst.
- ~20% 429s are our API gateway rejecting due to per-customer burst limit; some of those originate from repeat retries.
- There is a retry storm pattern from a handful of client IPs — exponential backoff isn't configured correctly on their side.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:30 PST):
- Enabled warm-capacity override for FableShop and routed traffic to their Dedicated pool (increased capacity x3).
- Shortened default KV-cache TTL to reduce memory pressure on heavy-generation requests.
- Throttled flagged client IPs at the edge to reduce retry amplification.
- Fail-open policy toggled for non-critical endpoints to return cached answers where possible.

Next actions (30–90 mins):
- Roll small canary of a smaller model variant for short requests (<128 tokens) to reduce OOM risk.
- Provide a temporary ramp guidance doc to FableShop: recommended ramp rate (60% of expected), suggested client backoff.
- Gathering metric screenshots for postmortem.

I'll keep you updated — will attach traces and a short packet of logs in 15.

Laura Bennett
SRE Lead, Runtime Reliability

Claire — wrapping up the incident and next steps (post-mortem draft attached):
- Timeline: brief surge at 08:05 PST on Nov 29, mitigations applied by 08:30 PST, p95 returned to target by 09:00 PST.
- Root cause: sudden press-driven concurrency spike exposing memory pressure on the chosen large-attention variant + client-side retry amplification hitting gateway burst guards.
- Short-term mitigations we applied: warm capacity override, model-fallback for short requests, IP-level soft-throttles, shortened cache TTLs.
- Recommendations for future press/ramp windows:
  * Submit ramp plan 48 hours prior using the shared ramp template (see attached ramp-plan-nov29.pdf).
  * Limit initial ramp to 60% of expected traffic for first 10 minutes, then stepwise increase (20% increments per 5 minutes) while monitoring 95th percentile latency.
  * Use the smaller-generation model for high concurrency short requests; enable client-side exponential backoff with jitter and max 2 retries.
  * Coordinate with our SREs if you anticipate >200k requests/min — we can provision burst capacity and a temporary SLA tweak.

We've attached the postmortem and logs: fableshop-logs-1129.zip. We'll schedule a technical review for Wednesday. Thanks for patience and quick coordination.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
